We answer this question affirmatively, for diagonalizability over either [MATH] or [MATH]. The main observation is a general principle: every semialgebraic property of a fixed-dimensional bounded mean parameter is eventually almost surely predictable. We give a self-contained shrinking-confidence-set proof and an explicit predictor obtained from polynomial sign tests. Tarski--Seidenberg quantifier elimination shows that both the real- and complex-diagonalizable loci are semialgebraic, despite being neither closed nor open. We further extend the positive result to unbounded observations with any fixed finite moment of order [MATH], using the Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund strong law. Combined with the Dembo--Peres topological criterion, this yields a sharp contrast: over the class of all merely integrable matrix laws, diagonalizability is not eventually almost surely predictable when the dimension is at least two. The construction is effective for fixed dimension, although no practical complexity bound is claimed.
tldr: This paper proves that diagonalizability of a mean binary matrix is eventually almost surely predictable from i.i.d. samples, using semialgebraic geometry and statistical learning theory.
motivation: The authors address a question by Wu and Santhanam about whether one can determine diagonalizability of an unknown mean matrix from random samples with finite error.
method: They establish a general principle that semialgebraic properties of bounded mean parameters are eventually predictable, using shrinking-confidence-set proofs and polynomial sign tests, with Tarski-Seidenberg quantifier elimination.
result: They affirmatively answer the question for real and complex diagonalizability, extend to unbounded observations with finite moments, and show a sharp contrast for merely integrable laws in dimension at least two.
conclusion: The work provides a definitive characterization of predictability for this property, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: High-order Energy-stable And Charge-conservative Lagrangian Fem For 3d Incompressible Inductionless Mhd Equations With Variable Density
authors: Lingxiao Li, Bijie Song, Haiyan Su, Jie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the solution of variable-density, incompressible inductionless magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations with moving interface. We propose a high-order, energy-stable and charge-conservative mixed finite element method in the Lagrangian framework. The method utilizes the moving high-order curved mesh techniques to resolve the interface, together with the second-order Backward Differentiation Formula (BDF2) for the temporal discretization of the velocity field and the second-order Adams--Bashforth method (AB2) for the update of control points of the meshes. High-order isoparametric Taylor-Hood element with grad-div stabilization are used for the velocity-pressure pair. Moreover, to ensure the discrete charge conservation, high-order parametric H(div)-conforming BDM element is adopted for the current density. We establish the unconditional discrete energy-stability for the fully discrete scheme. Numerical experiments validate the high-order accuracy and unconditional energy stability of the algorithm.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order finite element method for incompressible inductionless MHD equations with variable density, focusing on numerical stability and charge conservation.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a robust numerical method for simulating variable-density, incompressible inductionless MHD flows with moving interfaces, which is important in engineering applications.
method: They propose a mixed finite element method in a Lagrangian framework, using high-order curved meshes, BDF2 for velocity, AB2 for mesh control points, Taylor-Hood elements with grad-div stabilization, and H(div)-conforming BDM elements for current density.
result: The method achieves unconditional discrete energy stability and high-order accuracy, validated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for solving the considered MHD equations, ensuring energy stability and charge conservation.

title: Tensor-normal Maximum Likelihood Estimation At The Operator-norm Sample Threshold
authors: Guang Cheng Hengzhi He
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be independent Gaussian tensors in [MATH] whose covariance is a Kronecker product of [MATH] unknown positive-definite factors, and put [MATH] and [MATH]. A recent result of Franks et al. (2026) established condition-number-free nonasymptotic guarantees for the tensor-normal maximum likelihood estimator under the sample threshold [MATH]. They asked whether the cubic dependence on [MATH] could be replaced by the operator-norm scale [MATH]. We answer this question affirmatively. We prove that, for [MATH], the maximum likelihood estimator exists uniquely with high probability whenever [MATH], and satisfies [MATH] and [MATH]. For every mode of largest dimension, we also obtain the sharp Thompson bound [MATH]. No sparsity, condition-number bound or warm start is assumed. For fixed [MATH], the threshold has the information-theoretically optimal dependence on [MATH], and the displayed rates for the full precision and the largest factor match Gaussian minimax lower bounds up to a factor [MATH]. The proof extends a random Gram bound for local group-orbit directions to the full local Lie algebra, transports it to a fixed Thompson ball by exact conjugation, and combines sensitivity of a constrained maximum likelihood estimator with an equivariant Kirszbraun extension and Gaussian concentration. This removes the Frobenius-to-operator loss responsible for the previous extra factor [MATH] and resolves the explicit open problem posed in the earlier work.
tldr: This paper resolves an open problem in tensor-normal maximum likelihood estimation, proving optimal sample complexity and rates without condition-number assumptions.
motivation: The paper addresses a theoretical question in high-dimensional statistics about the sample threshold for tensor-normal MLE, aiming to improve existing bounds.
method: The proof extends a random Gram bound to the full local Lie algebra, uses exact conjugation to a Thompson ball, and combines sensitivity analysis with an equivariant Kirszbraun extension and Gaussian concentration.
result: For p ≥ C n log n, the MLE exists uniquely with high probability and achieves optimal rates matching minimax lower bounds up to a constant factor.
conclusion: The results resolve the open problem and provide sharp guarantees for tensor-normal MLE, advancing statistical theory.

title: Indefinite Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control Problem For A Markov Regime-Switching Model
authors: Na Li, Yilin Wei, Harry Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates an indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic (SLQ) control problem with parameters subject to Markov regime-switching. Based on the well-posedness of the SLQ problem, we introduce a relaxed compensator that extends SLQ control problems from the positive definite case to the indefinite case. We analyze the corresponding stochastic Hamiltonian system for both unconstrained and constrained control cases under the indefinite framework and derive the corresponding optimal open-loop controls. We further investigate the associated Riccati equations for both unconstrained and constrained control cases and derive the closed-loop feedback forms of optimal controls. We illustrate the theoretical results with an equity-bond asset allocation problem under un-constrained and non-negative control constraints. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the theoretical framework and demonstrate its practical value in solving complex stochastic control problems with Markov regime-switching.
tldr: This paper studies an indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problem with Markov regime-switching, deriving optimal controls and Riccati equations.
motivation: The paper aims to extend SLQ control theory to indefinite cases with regime-switching, which is a mathematical finance and control theory problem.
method: The authors introduce a relaxed compensator, analyze the stochastic Hamiltonian system, and derive Riccati equations for both unconstrained and constrained cases.
result: They obtain open-loop and closed-loop optimal controls and validate with numerical simulations on an equity-bond allocation problem.
conclusion: The framework effectively handles indefinite SLQ problems with regime-switching, demonstrating practical value in stochastic control.

title: A Numerical Approach For Solving The time-Fractional Mobile-Immobile Transport Equation
authors: Sandip Maji
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional diffusion models provide a powerful framework for describing anomalous transport phenomena in heterogeneous porous media. The Mobile-Immobile model is a fundamental approach for characterizing such anomalous diffusion, specifically addressing the delayed solute transport caused by mass transfer between mobile and immobile regions. In this study, we develop and analyze two fully discrete numerical schemes for the one-dimensional time-fractional Mobile-Immobile model governed by the Caputo derivative of order [MATH]. The spatial discretization is carried out using a non-symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method, while the temporal derivative is approximated by the Crank-Nicolson L1 and L2-[MATH] formulas, resulting in two distinct schemes with high-order accuracy. Rigorous stability and error analyses are established, showing that the methods achieve optimal convergence rates depending on the regularity of the exact solution. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed schemes. The presented framework provides a reliable and accurate approach for simulating complex fractional transport processes in porous media and related fields.
tldr: This paper develops numerical schemes for a time-fractional mobile-immobile transport equation, which is a topic in applied mathematics and porous media modeling, unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to provide accurate numerical methods for simulating anomalous transport in porous media, which is important in hydrology and environmental engineering.
method: The authors use a non-symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for spatial discretization and Crank-Nicolson L1 and L2-1σ formulas for temporal discretization, and they analyze stability and convergence.
result: The proposed schemes achieve optimal convergence rates and are verified by numerical experiments, demonstrating efficiency and robustness.
conclusion: The framework offers a reliable approach for simulating fractional transport processes, but it has no connection to quantum information or related fields.

title: Pure Matrix States On Block Toeplitz Matrices
authors: Ritul Duhan Tirthankar Bhattacharyya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] denote the operator system of all block Toeplitz matrices [MATH] with entries [MATH] % T_{k} = \left[ t^{(k)}_{p-q} \right]_{p,q=1}^m. \[ T = T_0 & T_{-1} & \cdots & T_{-(n-1)} T_1 & T_0 & \cdots & T_{-(n-2)} \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots T_{n-1} & T_{n-2}& \cdots & T_0 \in M_{mn}(). \] We characterize all pure unital completely positive ({}) maps from [MATH] to [MATH]. Working through the Stinespring isometry [MATH] and the matrix-valued polynomial [MATH], we prove that [MATH] is pure if and only if it admits a unique pure \ucp extension to [MATH] if and only if [MATH] has degree [MATH] with all its roots on the unit circle [MATH]. Every such pure [MATH] induces a \ucp map [MATH] on [MATH] given by \[ \Phi_{Q_V}(f) = \int_{} Q_V(z)^* f(z) Q_V(z)\, dz. \] Let [MATH] be the compact convex set of all \ucp maps from [MATH] to [MATH]. Endowing [MATH] with the matricial Monge-Kantorovich metric [MATH], via an analysis of the extreme points of [MATH] together with a point-splitting lemma, we show that the induced maps as above are [MATH]-dense in [MATH]. Consequently, if [MATH] denotes the set of normalized [MATH] where [MATH] is as above, then the Hausdorff distance [MATH] as [MATH], extending known results of approximation of positive regular Borel measures on the unit circle to the setting of matrix-valued completely positive maps.
tldr: This paper characterizes pure unital completely positive maps on block Toeplitz matrices and shows density of induced maps in the matricial Monge-Kantorovich metric.
motivation: The work extends classical approximation results for measures on the unit circle to the setting of matrix-valued completely positive maps, aiming to understand the structure of pure UCP maps on operator systems of block Toeplitz matrices.
method: The authors use Stinespring isometries and matrix-valued polynomials to characterize purity, and employ extreme point analysis and a point-splitting lemma to prove density in the matricial Monge-Kantorovich metric.
result: They prove that a UCP map is pure iff it has a unique pure extension iff the associated polynomial has degree with all roots on the unit circle, and that the induced maps are dense in the set of all UCP maps.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete characterization of pure UCP maps on block Toeplitz matrices and establishes a density result, extending known measure approximation results to the noncommutative setting.

title: Uniform Discrete Poincar\'e Inequalities For Hybrid High-Order Differential Forms On Polyhedral Meshes
authors: Silvano Pitassi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Hybrid High-Order framework for differential forms on general polyhedral meshes. For each form degree [MATH], the discrete space combines polynomial differential forms on mesh cells with polynomial trace unknowns on mesh faces, and the exterior derivative is reconstructed through a local Stokes formula. In three dimensions, the corresponding vector proxies recover the usual hybrid gradient, curl, and divergence reconstructions, while the differential-form setting provides a unified exterior-calculus generalisation in arbitrary space dimension. Within this framework, we prove uniform discrete Poincar\'e inequalities at every form degree. The canonical broken--stabilised seminorm controls the distance, in the hybrid [MATH] norm, to the full kernel of the prescribed reconstructed exterior derivative, uniformly with respect to the mesh size and to every stability-admissible choice of the face spaces. The result holds on domains with arbitrary topology.
tldr: This paper introduces a Hybrid High-Order framework for differential forms on polyhedral meshes, proving uniform discrete Poincaré inequalities.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize hybrid high-order methods to differential forms in arbitrary dimensions, providing a unified framework and stability results.
method: The authors construct discrete spaces combining polynomial forms on cells and faces, reconstruct the exterior derivative via local Stokes formula, and prove uniform Poincaré inequalities.
result: They prove uniform discrete Poincaré inequalities for all form degrees, with constants independent of mesh size and face space choices, on domains with arbitrary topology.
conclusion: This work contributes to numerical analysis of differential forms, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Locking Analysis And High-order Locking-free Finite Element Method For Three-dimensional Electroporoelasticity Equations
authors: Xuan Liu, Yongkui Zou, Yanzhao Cao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroporoelasticity equations couple Maxwell's equations with Biot's poroelasticity model and admit severe Poisson locking in standard conforming finite element discretizations when the Lam\'e constant is large. In this paper, we provide a rigorous analysis of the Poisson locking phenomenon for three-dimensional quasi-static electroporoelasticity equations and show that the spatial convergence order of conforming finite element approximations is reduced in the nearly incompressible regime. To eliminate this locking effect, we introduce a five-field formulation and a fully discrete high-order finite element method. We prove uniform stability with respect to large Lam\'e constant. Based on this, we establish a locking-free scheme by deriving its uniform error estimates with respect to the Lam\'e coefficient. The analysis covers the fully coupled electromagnetic-poroelastic system and applies to high-order elements in three dimensions. Extensive numerical experiments are presented to verify the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate robustness with respect to the Lam\'e parameter.
tldr: This paper analyzes Poisson locking in finite element methods for electroporoelasticity equations and proposes a locking-free high-order method.
motivation: The paper addresses numerical challenges in solving coupled electromagnetic-poroelastic systems, which are not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors provide a rigorous locking analysis and introduce a five-field formulation with a fully discrete high-order finite element method, proving uniform stability and error estimates.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed method eliminates Poisson locking and achieves uniform convergence rates independent of the Lamé constant, verified by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work contributes to computational mechanics but has no connection to quantum information science or related fields.

title: Adaptive Time-Stepping Euler--Maruyama Scheme For SDEs With Non-Globally Lipschitz Coefficients: Uniform Convergence, Stability And Ergodicity
authors: Xueqi Wen, Shan Huang, Xiaoyue Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops an adaptive time-stepping Euler--Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with non-globally Lipschitz drift and diffusion coefficients. By dynamically adjusting the timestep at each iteration, the proposed scheme effectively prevents numerical instability. We prove the moment boundedness of the numerical solution and establish a [MATH]-order strong convergence rate both on finite-time intervals and uniformly in time. Furthermore, the scheme faithfully inherits the [MATH]th moment exponential stability of the underlying SDE. For long-time ergodic dynamics, we establish the polynomial ergodicity of the numerical invariant measure. Moreover, we show that the numerical invariant measure converges to the invariant measure of the underlying SDE at an optimal rate of [MATH] in the [MATH]-Wasserstein distance. Numerical experiments confirm our theoretical results and indicate the superior accuracy and computational performance of the proposed scheme over several fixed-step and existing adaptive methods.
tldr: This paper develops an adaptive time-stepping Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with non-globally Lipschitz coefficients, proving convergence, stability, and ergodicity.
motivation: The paper addresses numerical stability issues in simulating SDEs with non-globally Lipschitz coefficients, which are common in finance and physics.
method: The authors propose an adaptive time-stepping Euler-Maruyama scheme that adjusts the timestep dynamically to prevent instability, and analyze its theoretical properties.
result: They establish moment boundedness, strong convergence rates, preservation of exponential stability, and polynomial ergodicity of the numerical invariant measure, with optimal convergence in Wasserstein distance.
conclusion: The adaptive scheme offers superior accuracy and computational performance compared to fixed-step methods, as confirmed by numerical experiments.

title: Robust Unit Commitment In District Heating Networks: Chance-Constrained And CVaR Optimization Under Demand Uncertainty
authors: Annika Buchholz, Janina Zittel, Thorsten Koch
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While district heating networks are a key component of the energy transition, their operational planning is challenging due to substantial uncertainty in heat demand. We address this volatility without compromising system reliability. By adapting chance-constrained programming (CC) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) optimization to the mixed-integer unit-commitment problem for district-heating networks, we can compute optimal unit-commitment schedules under demand uncertainty. We generate heat demand time series using a Bayesian model, which explicitly quantifies forecasting uncertainty and yields predictive distributions as input to the network optimization. To handle the inherent uncertainty in heat demand, we apply both robust optimization approaches: chance-constrained programming limits the probability of unmet demand, while CVaR optimization penalizes severe shortfalls in the tail of the distribution. We evaluate the approaches both on real-world data from the Berlin district heating network and on a benchmark set of synthetic, realistically parameterized instances of varying sizes. The results compare the two uncertainty-handling methods with respect to solution quality, risk exposure, and computational effort.
tldr: This paper applies chance-constrained and CVaR optimization to unit commitment in district heating networks under demand uncertainty.
motivation: District heating networks face operational challenges due to uncertain heat demand, and robust optimization methods are needed to ensure reliability.
method: The authors adapt chance-constrained programming and CVaR optimization to a mixed-integer unit-commitment problem, using Bayesian models to generate demand forecasts.
result: The methods are evaluated on real Berlin data and synthetic instances, comparing solution quality, risk exposure, and computational effort.
conclusion: The paper provides robust scheduling approaches for district heating, but it is not related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Safe Observation Capacity For Opponent Exploitation Under Showdown Censoring
authors: Jiaxing Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.09954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In poker-like games, folds hide private cards, so showdown data are missing not at random. The usual per-card estimator converges to a selected distribution, and its confidence sets can lose coverage as the sample grows. A floor-safe probe changes the monitoring process: it drives a chosen line to showdown, reveals every non-fold continuation, and uses sequence-form flow to recover censored fold mass on reveal-certified histories. We price this repair through safe observation capacity [MATH], the largest floor-safe reach rate at safety budget [MATH]. Its frontier is concave and piecewise linear, with origin slope equal to the floor's shadow price. When one-hand reveal mass factorizes into safe reach and opponent continuation, matching bounds give conditional per-target cost [MATH] for a local censored-fiber direction. Safe Active De-censoring (SAD) combines capacity with public-anomaly routing and robust deployment; routing across targets remains heuristic. Evidence spans bucketed turn-river endgames, controlled instances, and a fixed-board unbucketed river subgame. In the latter, a constructed public twin admits a floor-safe response of value [MATH]; the audited public channel certifies only the blueprint floor, while population reveal evidence certifies at least [MATH] of [MATH]. Across a broader synthetic opponent population, public and solved grouped reveal fibers certify median shares of [MATH] and [MATH] of the safe-exploitable gap. Independent floor audits cover every evaluated probe and response. The results separate unconditional safety from the conditional statistical value of active reveal.
tldr: This paper introduces a method for safely estimating opponent strategies in poker-like games with censored showdown data, using a floor-safe probe and sequence-form flow to recover missing information.
motivation: In poker-like games, folds censor private cards, leading to biased estimates and unreliable confidence sets. The authors aim to correct this by actively driving lines to showdown while respecting safety constraints.
method: The paper defines safe observation capacity, a concave piecewise-linear frontier, and proposes Safe Active De-censoring (SAD) that combines capacity with public-anomaly routing and robust deployment to recover censored fold mass.
result: Experiments on bucketed turn-river endgames and a fixed-board river subgame show that the method can certify a significant fraction of the safe-exploitable gap, with independent floor audits validating the probes.
conclusion: The results separate unconditional safety from conditional statistical value, demonstrating that active reveal can improve opponent exploitation while maintaining safety guarantees.

title: Exploiting Structure In The Boolean Weighted Constraint Satisfaction Problem: A Constraint Composite Graph-Based Approach
authors: Hong Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What is "structure," and how can we exploit it in combinatorial optimization? Reasoning tasks such as system design, state estimation, and prediction can be cast as combinatorial optimization problems (COPs), traditionally attacked by dedicated algorithms that fail outside their narrow subclass, while communities working on equivalent problems reinvent each other's techniques. The weighted constraint satisfaction problem (WCSP) is a general framework that subsumes COPs from many communities and represents complex physical and non-physical systems, from spin glasses to social networks. Is such generality a curse? Our answer is to exploit "structure": a general-purpose WCSP algorithm should automatically imitate the specialized algorithm for whatever subclass its input belongs to. A WCSP has macro (graphical) structure, which variables interact, and micro (numerical) structure, how they interact. Separate schools of thought exploit one or the other, never both. The constraint composite graph (CCG), introduced in 2008, unifies them: it is an undirected graph over a WCSP instance's variables plus auxiliary ones, on which minimum weighted vertex cover (MWVC) solves the original instance. It is efficiently constructible, but largely unexploited. This dissertation answers three questions affirmatively. The CCG has theoretical advantages beyond identifying tractable classes (new properties proved here); it is practically useful (efficient implementation and experiments); and it extends promisingly to non-Boolean variables (new encodings). We use the CCG to (a) kernelize a WCSP instance, fixing optimal values of some variables by maxflow before search begins, (b) improve min-sum message passing, (c) exploit integer linear programming solvers, and (d) solve COPs on quantum annealers. Solving general COPs faster classically also yields better baselines for the debated quantum advantage.
tldr: This paper explores exploiting structure in the Boolean Weighted Constraint Satisfaction Problem (WCSP) using a Constraint Composite Graph (CCG) to improve solving efficiency and enable quantum annealing.
motivation: The paper aims to address the challenge of solving general combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) by exploiting both graphical and numerical structure, which is often ignored by specialized algorithms.
method: The author introduces the Constraint Composite Graph (CCG) that unifies macro and micro structure, and uses it for kernelization, improving message passing, leveraging ILP solvers, and mapping to quantum annealers.
result: The dissertation claims theoretical advantages, practical efficiency, and extensions to non-Boolean variables, with experiments demonstrating improved performance.
conclusion: The CCG approach offers a promising general-purpose method for solving WCSPs, with potential implications for classical and quantum computing.

title: MarkNull: Model-Agnostic Watermark Removal In AI-Generated Images Via On-Manifold Latent Manipulation
authors: Jie Cao, Qi Li, Zelin Zhang, Xiaodong Wu, Lingshuang Liu, Xiangman Li, Jianbing Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital watermarking has emerged as a critical technique for provenance and copyright attribution in AI-generated imagery, yet its robustness against realistic, model-agnostic removal attacks remains poorly explored. Existing attacks either succeed only against specific generative models or achieve removal at the cost of severe visual degradation. In this paper, we propose MarkNull, a model-agnostic watermark removal attack via on-manifold latent manipulation. MarkNull is grounded in a key observation: watermarked images exhibit a strong statistical dependency between the generated latent representation and the embedded initial noise. To quantify this dependency, we introduce the Noise-Latent Alignment Score (NLAS) and formulate an optimization objective that selectively decorrelates the latent representation from the embedded watermark while preserving semantic fidelity. Extensive evaluations across different categories of watermarking paradigms, including post-hoc, fine-tuning-based, and initial-noise-based schemes, demonstrate that MarkNull reduces average bit accuracy to 53.14%, approaching random-guessing (50%), without perceptible image degradation. To further improve scalability, we propose MarkNull-A, an amortized, optimization-free variant that distills the attack into a single forward pass, achieving 0.50 s/image with modest computational overhead. Notably, our attacks successfully compromise Google's SynthID-Image system while preserving high visual quality and transfer effectively to video watermarking. Finally, we present an attack detection mechanism as a defensive counterpart to MarkNull and MarkNull-A, highlighting the necessity of developing watermark designs resilient to model-agnostic latent-space attacks.
tldr: This paper introduces MarkNull, a model-agnostic watermark removal attack on AI-generated images via on-manifold latent manipulation, and a defensive detection mechanism.
motivation: Existing watermark removal attacks are either model-specific or cause visual degradation, and the robustness of watermarks against realistic attacks is poorly explored.
method: MarkNull quantifies the statistical dependency between latent representations and embedded noise using a Noise-Latent Alignment Score (NLAS) and optimizes to decorrelate the latent from the watermark while preserving semantics. An amortized variant, MarkNull-A, distills the attack into a single forward pass.
result: MarkNull reduces average bit accuracy to 53.14% (near random guessing) across various watermarking schemes, including Google's SynthID-Image, without perceptible degradation, and transfers to video watermarking.
conclusion: The work highlights vulnerabilities in current watermarking and proposes a detection mechanism, emphasizing the need for more resilient watermark designs.

title: Beyond Detection Accuracy: Measuring Explanation Cost, Stability, And Utility For Resource-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection
authors: Abdurrahman Tolay
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning intrusion-detection studies commonly emphasize predictive accuracy while treating explanation generation as a computationally free post-processing step. This study jointly evaluates predictive effectiveness, explanation cost, local explanation stability, and selective explanation for binary Internet of Things (IoT) intrusion detection. A leakage-safe CICIoT2023 corpus was constructed using exact 39-feature hashes, non-finite-value handling, exact-feature deduplication, conservative label-collision removal, and deterministic hash-level partitioning. Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated on natural and balanced test distributions. TreeSHAP cost was measured, stability was assessed under prediction-preserving perturbations, and validation-calibrated policies were used to allocate explanation workload. XGBoost provided the strongest overall predictive profile, while Random Forest produced the lowest false-positive rate. At 5,000 samples, TreeSHAP required 700.759 s for Random Forest and 1.471 s for XGBoost. Random Forest showed the strongest overall base-level explanation stability; XGBoost retained high rank and directional consistency but showed greater top-feature turnover and attribution-magnitude drift. On the balanced test, about 90% false-negative explanation coverage permitted 28-32% compute savings, while about 95% coverage permitted 15-23% savings. Savings were much smaller under the attack-heavy natural prevalence. These results show that operationally useful explainable IoT intrusion detection depends on predictive quality, explanation cost, local stability, workload prevalence, and selective invocation rather than detection accuracy alone.
tldr: This paper evaluates explainable AI for IoT intrusion detection, focusing on explanation cost, stability, and selective invocation, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The study addresses the gap in intrusion detection research that often ignores the computational cost and stability of explanations, aiming to provide a more comprehensive evaluation for resource-aware IoT security.
method: The authors construct a leakage-safe CICIoT2023 dataset and evaluate Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost on natural and balanced test sets, measuring TreeSHAP cost, stability under perturbations, and using validation-calibrated policies for selective explanation.
result: XGBoost had the best predictive profile, Random Forest had the lowest false-positive rate, and selective explanation could save 28-32% compute at 90% coverage on balanced data, with smaller savings under natural prevalence.
conclusion: Operationally useful explainable IoT intrusion detection requires balancing predictive quality, explanation cost, stability, and selective invocation, not just accuracy.

title: Non-Existence Of Efx Chore Allocations For Monotone Cost Functions With Binary Marginals
authors: Zehan Lin, Shengxin Liu, Biaoshuai Tao, Shengwei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the existence of envy-free up to any item (EFX) allocations of indivisible chores when agents have monotone cost functions with binary marginals. For indivisible goods, the corresponding existence question is known to have an affirmative answer for general monotone functions with binary marginals. For chores, however, the existence of EFX allocation was previously known only for more restricted classes, while the general binary-marginal case remained unresolved. In this paper, we provide two counterexamples based on the same 18-agent, 53-chore word gadget, with one cost profile for binary XOS costs and another for binary supermodular costs. In both cases, a complete EFX allocation need not exist. Finally, we formalize and verify our main results in Lean 4.
tldr: This paper studies the existence of envy-free up to any item (EFX) allocations for chores with monotone cost functions having binary marginals, providing counterexamples showing non-existence in certain cases.
motivation: The existence of EFX allocations for chores with binary marginals was an open question, as prior results only covered restricted classes. The authors aim to resolve this by constructing counterexamples.
method: The authors construct an 18-agent, 53-chore word gadget and provide two cost profiles: one for binary XOS costs and one for binary supermodular costs. They then prove that no complete EFX allocation exists for these profiles, and verify the results using the Lean 4 proof assistant.
result: They show that EFX allocations need not exist for chores with monotone cost functions having binary marginals, even for binary XOS and binary supermodular cost functions.
conclusion: The paper settles the existence question negatively for these classes, highlighting a fundamental limitation in fair division of chores.

title: Mixed Choice Multiparty Session Types, Precisely
authors: Nobuko Yoshida Jake Masters
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A precise (sound and complete) subtyping relation [MATH] specifies that [MATH] is a subtype of [MATH] if and only if a program of type [MATH] can always safely replace a program of type [MATH] without compromising the safety of a larger program. This paper formulates and proves preciseness of subtyping for mixed choice multiparty session types with session delegation, creation, and interleaving. We prove soundness by developing the first general type system for a full mixed choice multiparty session [MATH]-calculus. To prove completeness, we introduce the three-party lock, which is a minimal and general form of liveness error for handling interleaved sessions, and we establish a new proof technique based on a construction of scheduler processes which enable exhaustive detection for all failures of the subtyping relation. We then extend the preciseness results to a family of mixed choice multiparty session types. Algorithms for checking (1) subtyping and (2) safety, deadlock-freedom, and liveness of typing contexts are fully implemented and optimised to run in quadratic time with respect to the size of the state space and typing context, and have been evaluated with (mixed choice) case studies from the literature.
tldr: This paper presents a precise subtyping relation for mixed choice multiparty session types, with soundness and completeness proofs and efficient algorithms.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a sound and complete subtyping relation for mixed choice multiparty session types, which is important for type-safe session-based concurrency.
method: The authors develop a general type system for a full mixed choice multiparty session π-calculus, introduce the three-party lock to handle liveness errors, and construct scheduler processes for exhaustive detection of subtyping failures.
result: They prove preciseness (soundness and completeness) of subtyping and extend results to a family of session types. Algorithms for subtyping and safety checking are implemented and run in quadratic time.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational result for session types, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Search-to-Decision Reductions For The Linear And General Code Equivalence Problems
authors: Abhinaba Mazumder
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present efficient search-to-decision reductions for the Linear Code Equivalence (LCE) and Generalised Code Equivalence (GCE) problems. Our methodology is inspired by the recent search-to-decision reduction for Permutation Code Equivalence. We demonstrate how to recover the permutation component of the equivalence using a decision oracle, and subsequently show one way of recovering the diagonal and field automorphism components in deterministic polynomial time by leveraging the elegant Engel-Schneider algorithm for diagonal equivalence.
tldr: This paper presents search-to-decision reductions for the Linear and Generalised Code Equivalence problems, which are computational problems in coding theory.
motivation: The paper aims to establish the equivalence between search and decision versions of code equivalence problems, which are important in post-quantum cryptography.
method: The methodology adapts a recent search-to-decision reduction for Permutation Code Equivalence, using a decision oracle to recover the permutation component and then applying the Engel-Schneider algorithm to recover diagonal and field automorphism components.
result: The paper demonstrates efficient reductions, showing that solving the decision problem allows recovery of the full equivalence in deterministic polynomial time.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theoretical understanding of code equivalence problems, potentially impacting cryptographic security assessments.

title: Twisted Conjugacy And The Classification Of Induced Centrosymmetric Alternant Codes
authors: Massamba Sow Ousmane Ndiaye
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a classification of induced centrosymmetric alternant codes through the study of the automorphism structures inherited from Generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes. We introduce the twisted conjugation action naturally associated with projective semilinear transformations and establish its correspondence with ordinary conjugacy in the projective semilinear group. This correspondence enables the application of Shintani's theorem to classify the [MATH]-similarity classes of involutions. As a consequence, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for an alternant code to admit a centrosymmetric structure induced by a projective semilinear automorphism. The resulting classification unifies the different families of induced centrosymmetric alternant codes within a common automorphism-based framework.
tldr: This paper classifies induced centrosymmetric alternant codes using twisted conjugacy and projective semilinear transformations, with no connection to quantum information.
motivation: The paper aims to classify a family of error-correcting codes by studying their automorphism structures, which is a topic in classical coding theory.
method: The authors introduce a twisted conjugation action associated with projective semilinear transformations and use Shintani's theorem to classify similarity classes of involutions.
result: They obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for an alternant code to admit a centrosymmetric structure induced by a projective semilinear automorphism, unifying families of such codes.
conclusion: The classification provides a common automorphism-based framework for induced centrosymmetric alternant codes, but it is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A New Characteristic-Uniform Model For Elliptic Curves -- Theory, Arithmetic, And Applications
authors: Hongfeng Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.01675v4 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a characteristic-uniform arithmetic theory for \[ \mathcal C_d:\quad (u^2+u)(v^2+v)=d. \] For \(d(1-16d)\ne0\), its smooth \((2,2)\)-completion has four rational boundary points forming \(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\), an intrinsic \(D_8\)-action, the inverse \(-(u,v)=(u,-v-1)\), and the native Kummer map \(\kappa_d(u,v)=(u+1)\). Working natively, we derive complete full-point and differential laws, Kummer ladders and recovery, halving, tripling, \(2P+Q\), division polynomials, isogenies, CM endomorphisms, and pairings, with dedicated formulas in characteristics two and three. Classical models provide proof and optimization dictionaries while all endpoints remain native. For Cd25519, the Kummer line is exactly the X25519 line, and a native Segre recoding realizes the optimized complete \(a=-1\) Edwards full-point dependency graph. We further study \[ \mathcal C_{a,b,d}:(u^2+u+a)(v^2+v+b)=d,\quad \mathcal T_{a,d}:(u^2+u+a)(v^2+v)=d,\\ \mathcal R_{\tau,\sigma,\kappa}:(x^2-\tau)(y^2-\sigma)=\kappa xy,\quad \mathcal Q_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}:x^2y^2+\alpha(x^2+y^2)+\beta xy+\gamma=0. \] For these product, one-sided twisted, reciprocal, and QRT families, we determine their genus-one geometry, finite-field forms, arithmetic, and isogenies. On each smooth QRT fibre, the Vieta--McMillan map is a fixed elliptic translation. Marking \(D\) gives the state \(P\mapsto(\kappa(P),\kappa(P+D))\), with maps realizing \(n\mapsto mn+r\). This yields logarithmic ladders and an elliptic Lucas calculus with nonlinear addition, fast-index doubling, state-division polynomials, and bridges to elliptic divisibility sequences, sigma functions, and elliptic nets. In characteristic two, every ordinary pointed elliptic curve over a perfect field admits the binary state model.
tldr: This paper develops a characteristic-uniform arithmetic theory for a family of elliptic curves, focusing on algebraic geometry and computational arithmetic, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a unified arithmetic framework for a specific family of elliptic curves, enabling efficient computations and applications in cryptography.
method: The author introduces a characteristic-uniform model for elliptic curves, derives complete arithmetic laws (point addition, scalar multiplication, isogenies, pairings), and studies several related curve families, providing formulas for characteristics two and three.
result: The paper presents a comprehensive arithmetic theory, including Kummer ladders, division polynomials, isogenies, and connections to elliptic divisibility sequences, with applications to cryptographic curves like Cd25519.
conclusion: The work contributes to elliptic curve arithmetic and cryptography, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests in quantum information and related fields.

title: A Pragmatic Guide To Building Conservative Discrete Abstractions Of Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Jordan Peper, Krish Kapadia, James Gast, Ethan Howes, Ivan Ruchkin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symbolic model checking is an effective approach for verifying semantically rich temporal-logic properties of cyber-physical systems, but it hinges on discretizing continuous-state dynamics into a finite-state abstraction. To transfer verification guarantees from the abstract model to the concrete CPS, the abstraction must conservatively approximate the concrete state space and behaviors. Hence, model-builders must maintain this soundness while balancing pessimism with tractability. However, they face several common pitfalls such as under-approximating the state space, under-approximating transitions, unsound pruning of "degenerate" behaviors, and improper specification lifting. This tutorial presents a pragmatic, conservative-by-construction workflow for building discrete abstractions of closed-loop dynamical systems. The workflow consists of four modular steps with interchangeable subroutines: (i) state-space partition and abstraction-function design, (ii) conservative transition construction via axis-aligned bounding boxes, polytopes, or sampling with PAC coverage certificates, (iii) mitigation of spurious transitions and self-loops using certified erasure and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement, and (iv) sound lifting of LTL specifications using may-must semantics. We demonstrate the end-to-end pipeline on three case studies and report how these design choices affect abstraction structure, runtime, and verification outcomes.
tldr: This paper is a tutorial on building conservative discrete abstractions for symbolic model checking of cyber-physical systems, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of verifying temporal-logic properties of cyber-physical systems by discretizing continuous dynamics, but this is outside the user's research interests.
method: It presents a four-step workflow for constructing conservative abstractions, including state-space partitioning, transition construction, spurious transition mitigation, and specification lifting.
result: The workflow is demonstrated on three case studies, showing how design choices affect abstraction structure, runtime, and verification outcomes.
conclusion: The paper provides practical guidance for building sound abstractions, but it is not relevant to the user's focus on quantum information and related fields.

title: Verdict: Training-Free Step-Wise Verification Of Multimodal Reasoning Via Disagreement-Aware Consensus
authors: Rohit Sinha, Kunal Tilaganji, Tanuja Ganu, Nagarajan Natarajan, Amit Sharma, Vineeth Balasubramanian
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10665v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models often generate reasoning chains containing subtle errors that lead to incorrect answers. Current verification approaches have notable limitations. Existing approaches either require expensive labelled supervision with inconsistent cross-task performance or aggregate scores from multiple sources by simple aggregations, missing a key insight: when these scores disagree, that disagreement itself carries important information about whether a reasoning step is truly valid or not. We formalise this as a coupled scoring problem among disparate, frozen verifiers, interpretable as a coordination game with a unique closed-form equilibrium where agreement signals valid steps while disagreement reveals instability. Towards this end, we propose a training-free domain-agnostic step-wise verification approach we call VERDICT: VERification via Disagreement-Informed Coupled Thresholding. To our knowledge, VERDICT is the first training-free verifier that makes the structure of cross-modal disagreement explicit and actionable. It computes consensus scores through a closed-form solution, enabling both disagreement-aware filtering and stability-conscious ranking of reasoning steps. Evaluated across six benchmarks, \method consistently improves over the base model by up to +5.95%, and performs competitively with domain-specific critics that demand extensive supervision, demonstrating that cross-modal agreement provides robust verification signals without task-specific adaptation and Training-Free Verification.
tldr: This paper proposes a training-free step-wise verification method for multimodal reasoning using disagreement-aware consensus among frozen verifiers.
motivation: Existing verification approaches for multimodal reasoning either require expensive supervision or fail to exploit disagreement among verifiers as a signal for validity.
method: VERDICT formulates verification as a coupled scoring problem among verifiers, solved via a closed-form equilibrium that combines agreement and disagreement to produce consensus scores for filtering and ranking reasoning steps.
result: Across six benchmarks, VERDICT improves over the base model by up to +5.95% and matches domain-specific critics without task-specific training.
conclusion: Cross-modal agreement provides robust verification signals, enabling effective training-free verification for multimodal reasoning.

title: Conversational Orchestration For Organic 6g
authors: Tarik Taleb Masoud Shokrnezhad
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Organic 6G vision of a network of networks spanning an edge-cloud continuum complemented by non-terrestrial resources requires, to realize its promise, service provisioning that is simple to operate, scalable across independently administered domains, and agile under domain churn (i.e., domains dynamically joining and leaving). Despite advances in cross-domain orchestration, many proposals rely on heavy integration fabrics, multi-layer coordinators, and deep telemetry pipelines that hinder deployability and amplify coordination overhead. We propose a lightweight, decentralized conversational orchestration framework based on Large Language Model (LLM)-driven domain agents. Each domain remains autonomous: an agent observes local state via tools, reasons in a closed loop, and exchanges summaries with neighboring agents over an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) overlay aligned with data-plane coupling. Fast feasible placement is enabled by periodic, routing-like dissemination of reachability advertisements (latency, bottleneck bandwidth, and compute capacity), while safe re-optimization, scaling, and migration are handled through event-driven requests and negotiation. To meet real-time constraints, we deploy a compact reasoning model trained with verifier-based self-verification and periodically refined online via shadow updates. Simulations show manageable, near-linear control-plane overhead as domains scale and during domain joins, and robust decision quality, including recovery after objective changes. We close by outlining future research directions for principled, secure, and uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration in Organic 6G.
tldr: This paper proposes a decentralized orchestration framework for 6G networks using LLM-driven agents, focusing on scalability and agility across domains.
motivation: The Organic 6G vision requires simple, scalable, and agile service provisioning across independently administered domains, but existing cross-domain orchestration approaches are heavy and complex.
method: The authors design a lightweight orchestration framework where each domain is managed by an LLM-based agent that observes local state, reasons, and exchanges summaries with neighbors over an A2A overlay. They use reachability advertisements for placement and event-driven negotiation for re-optimization, with a compact reasoning model trained via verifier-based self-verification and online shadow updates.
result: Simulations show manageable near-linear control-plane overhead and robust decision quality, including recovery after objective changes.
conclusion: The framework offers a promising direction for agentic orchestration in 6G, with future work on security and uncertainty awareness.

title: Enhanced Filtering Algorithms For The Euclidean Traveling Salesperson Problem And Its Variants In Constraint Logic Programming
authors: Marco Gavanelli Alessandro Bertagnon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) is one of the best-known problems in computer science and arises in many engineering applications, such as smart vehicles and intelligent transportation systems. In the "Euclidean" case, each node is defined by its coordinates in the plane and distances are computed using the Euclidean metric. In the Constraint Programming (CP) literature, the Euclidean TSP is typically addressed by computing the full distance matrix and treating it as a general case; however this approach ignores the geometric information carried by the points' coordinates. In this work, we propose new filtering algorithms, implemented in Constraint Logic Programming (CLP), that exploit such geometric information to achieve stronger constraint propagation than existing approaches. Moreover, we show how this methodology can be extended to other Euclidean variants of the TSP, including the Euclidean Generalized Traveling Salesperson Problem (EGTSP), which is relevant in practical routing and logistics applications. Experimental results demonstrate the computational advantages of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper proposes enhanced filtering algorithms for the Euclidean Traveling Salesperson Problem and its variants using Constraint Logic Programming, exploiting geometric information for stronger constraint propagation.
motivation: The Euclidean TSP is important in engineering applications, but existing CP approaches ignore geometric information, leading to weaker propagation.
method: The authors develop new filtering algorithms in CLP that use the coordinates of points to achieve stronger constraint propagation, and extend the methodology to Euclidean variants like the Generalized TSP.
result: Experimental results demonstrate computational advantages over existing approaches.
conclusion: The proposed geometric-aware filtering algorithms improve efficiency for Euclidean TSP variants in CP.

title: Strategies To Avoid Illegal Data Access
authors: Muhammad Mubeen, Arslan Bisharat, Giri Anandhi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For companies of all sizes, data security is a top priority. The chance of unauthorized data access increases as technology develops. To prevent unwanted access to their data, businesses must be proactive. This study examines technology solutions, personnel training, and policy enforcement as methods to prevent unauthorized data access. Data may be protected from illegal access using technological solutions like firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and encryption. Intrusion detection systems notify the administrator when suspicious behavior is found, while firewalls serve as a protective border between the internal network and the internet. Even if data is intercepted, encryption makes sure it is safe. Another effective method of avoiding unauthorized data access is employee education. Employees must be taught how to spot hazards like phishing emails and shady websites and react to them. Additionally, they should be taught the right way to utilize passwords and other security precautions. To secure data, organizations should create and implement policies. Policies should set out appropriate data and system use guidelines and provide repercussions for noncompliance. Policies should be evaluated regularly to ensure that they are current and useful. Businesses may prevent unwanted access to their data by installing technology solutions, training staff, and enforcing regulations. Organizations may reduce data breach risk and maintain regulatory compliance by taking these precautions. ...
tldr: This paper discusses general data security strategies such as firewalls, encryption, and employee training to prevent unauthorized access.
motivation: The authors aim to address the growing risk of unauthorized data access in companies by proposing proactive measures.
method: The study reviews technological solutions, personnel training, and policy enforcement as methods to prevent data breaches.
result: The paper suggests that combining these strategies can reduce data breach risk and maintain regulatory compliance.
conclusion: Organizations should implement a multi-layered approach including technology, training, and policies to protect data.

title: The Impact Of Cut-ins On Mixed-Autonomy Traffic Flow: Bridging Microscopic Game-Theoretic Model And Macroscopic Flow Analysis
authors: Yu Song
abstract: ArXiv:2608.09987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition to automated transportation introduces mixed-autonomy traffic where human drivers may strategically exploit the risk-averse behavior of Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs). While microscopic models capture these dyadic interactions, their aggregate impact on network-level stability remains unquantified due to the scale gap between agent-based and continuum models. This study bridges this analytical divide by integrating a game-theoretic friction term directly into the macroscopic kinematic wave framework. We model the cut-in maneuver as a Stackelberg game, identifying a distinct "exploitation window" where human drivers leverage CAV defensiveness to execute aggressive merges. By deriving a closed-form micro-macro bridge, we translate these discrete strategic outcomes into a continuous friction parameter that endogenously modifies the traffic conservation law. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations confirm that this behavioral asymmetry functions as a deterministic destabilizer, generating perturbation source terms that trigger phantom jams and strictly reduce road capacity. Crucially, we reveal a convex relationship between CAV penetration and system efficiency, identifying a critical instability regime at intermediate penetration rates (approximately 45 percent) where the frequency of exploitable interactions is maximized. These findings demonstrate that without socially aware control policies, the defensive nature of early-deployment CAVs may paradoxically degrade traffic flow stability.
tldr: This paper bridges microscopic game-theoretic models of cut-in maneuvers with macroscopic traffic flow analysis, showing that CAV defensive behavior can destabilize mixed-autonomy traffic.
motivation: The study aims to quantify the aggregate impact of strategic human-CAV interactions on network-level traffic stability, which is currently missing due to the scale gap between agent-based and continuum models.
method: The authors model cut-in as a Stackelberg game, derive a closed-form micro-macro bridge to translate discrete strategic outcomes into a continuous friction parameter, and integrate it into the kinematic wave framework.
result: The behavioral asymmetry acts as a deterministic destabilizer, generating perturbation sources that trigger phantom jams and reduce capacity, with a critical instability regime at ~45% CAV penetration.
conclusion: Without socially aware control policies, defensive CAVs may paradoxically degrade traffic flow stability, highlighting the need for such policies in mixed-autonomy systems.

title: Polyhedral Outer-Approximations For Misocp: Geometry And Cutting Planes
authors: Yongzheng Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-integer second-order cone programs are commonly solved by polyhedral outer approximation (OA), which iteratively strengthens a linear relaxation of the conic feasible region through cutting planes. We study how such approximations can be constructed more efficiently. First, we analyze the marginal contribution of a newly generated cut relative to cuts already present in the relaxation. Using violation- and volume-based measures, we show that this contribution decreases at least as fast as linearly as the new supporting direction approaches an existing one. Motivated by this geometric analysis, we develop a cut-generation strategy that balances separation depth with angular novelty and admits closed-form constructions. Second, we introduce a progressive-integrality OA framework that proceeds from an LP relaxation through partially integral relaxations before reaching the full MILP, thereby using inexpensive early iterations to strengthen the approximation before later mixed-integer solves. Computational experiments on CBLIB instances and large-scale AC unit-commitment models demonstrate complementary benefits from the proposed cut strategy and progressive integrality, substantially reducing the computational effort of outer approximation.
tldr: This paper focuses on polyhedral outer approximations for mixed-integer second-order cone programs, a topic in mathematical optimization with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to improve the efficiency of solving mixed-integer second-order cone programs, which are common in optimization problems, but this is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and related fields.
method: The authors analyze the marginal contribution of cutting planes and propose a cut-generation strategy balancing separation depth and angular novelty, along with a progressive-integrality outer approximation framework.
result: Computational experiments on CBLIB instances and AC unit-commitment models show that the proposed strategies reduce computational effort.
conclusion: The paper contributes to optimization methodology but has no relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Thread Scaling Of Hexaly On The Tdvrptw Across Two Model Encodings. An Experimental Report: External-Function Serialization, Slice-Count Choice, And The Time-Sliced Thread Ladder
authors: Florian Rascoussier
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thread scaling in Hexaly depends first on how the Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows is modeled. We compare two Python encodings: one evaluates continuous travel-time functions through external callbacks, while the other approximates them with time slices evaluated natively by the solver. Independent CPU measurements show that the supported external-function interface uses a single evaluator worker regardless of the requested thread count. The native encoding, by contrast, makes effective use of the allocated cores. Across our selected benchmark panel, wider native searches produce better solutions both at the end of the run and throughout the search, while substantially reducing variation between seeds. Nearly every paired run improves from one to sixteen threads. The choice of encoding has an even larger impact than the thread count: native evaluation provides the strongest gains, at the cost of a travel-time approximation that must be sufficiently fine and independently checked. These descriptive results support multi-threading as a practical way to improve solution quality and stability when the model can exploit it, and show that the modeling approach is central to thread-scaling conclusions in time-dependent routing.
tldr: This paper empirically studies thread scaling of the Hexaly solver on a time-dependent vehicle routing problem, comparing two model encodings, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how modeling choices affect thread scaling in a commercial optimization solver for a practical routing problem.
method: The authors compare two Python encodings of the TDVRPTW in Hexaly: one using external callbacks for continuous travel-time functions and another using time slices evaluated natively. They measure CPU usage and solution quality across thread counts from 1 to 16 on a benchmark panel.
result: The external-function interface uses a single evaluator worker regardless of thread count, while the native encoding scales effectively. Native encoding yields better solutions and lower variance, with nearly all paired runs improving from 1 to 16 threads.
conclusion: Modeling choice has a larger impact than thread count, and multi-threading improves solution quality when the model can exploit it, but this is specific to combinatorial optimization and not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Mathematical Modeling And Control Of Tuberculosis: Backward And Hopf Bifurcations Under Case-finding And Case-holding Interventions
authors: A. Schaberger, M. Actis, J. C. Bossio, A. H. Gonz\'alez, A. D Jorge
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinfection and relapse are known to induce backward bifurcation (a subcritical pitchfork bifurcation) in many infectious disease models, particularly tuberculosis. This phenomenon implies the coexistence of multiple equilibria when the basic reproduction number is below one: a stable disease-free equilibrium and two endemic equilibria, one stable and one unstable. As a result, hysteresis may arise, meaning that reducing the reproduction number below one may not eliminate the disease given that the system remains in the basin of attraction of the endemic state. Another relevant phenomenon, often associated with intervention delays, is the occurrence of supercritical Hopf bifurcations. In this case, the endemic equilibrium loses stability for reproduction numbers above one, leading to sustained oscillations in the form of stable limit cycles. Although less explored in the tuberculosis literature, this behavior has important implications for disease control. In this work, we analyze a tuberculosis model to investigate these dynamical effects and show that Hopf bifurcation can arise even without delays or saturation effects. The bifurcation analysis focuses on two key public health interventions -case finding and case holding- and their combined effect on disease dynamics. Numerical simulations, based on epidemiological data from Salta, Argentina -a province with high TB burden- illustrate the challenges these dynamics pose for the design and implementation of public health policies.
tldr: This paper models tuberculosis dynamics with backward and Hopf bifurcations under case-finding and case-holding interventions, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how reinfection and relapse cause backward bifurcation and how Hopf bifurcations can arise without delays, impacting TB control strategies.
method: They develop a mathematical model of TB transmission and perform bifurcation analysis, focusing on case-finding and case-holding interventions, with numerical simulations using data from Salta, Argentina.
result: The model exhibits backward bifurcation and Hopf bifurcations, leading to multiple equilibria and sustained oscillations, which complicate disease elimination.
conclusion: Public health policies must account for these dynamical complexities to effectively control TB.

title: An Optimal Energy Production Problem With Energy Source Switching And Load Following Nuclear Power Plants
authors: Fabio Baschetti, Alessandro Gnoatto, Athena Picarelli
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of weather-dependent renewable generation increases the volatility of residual demand and raises the value of dispatchable low-carbon flexibility. This paper studies the optimal operation of a load-following nuclear power plant owned by a producer that must balance stochastic residual demand while accounting for ramping limits and costly changes in operating regimes. Nuclear output can be increased, decreased, or kept constant, and the production decision is formulated as a finite-horizon optimal switching problem. We analyze both a closed-economy benchmark, where excess production cannot be sold and shortages require costly back-up generation, and an open-economy setting, where the producer can trade electricity at prices driven by aggregate market residual demand. The value functions are characterized as viscosity solutions of a system of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman quasi-variational inequalities, and optimal policies are computed using a monotone semi-Lagrangian scheme. The numerical results show how shortage costs, switching costs, ramping capability, and market access shape optimal nuclear load following. The analysis highlights the economic value of controllable low-carbon capacity in renewable-intensive systems and provides implications for flexibility remuneration, balancing-market design, and interconnection policy.
tldr: This paper studies optimal operation of load-following nuclear power plants using optimal switching and HJB equations, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The integration of renewable energy increases residual demand volatility, making dispatchable low-carbon flexibility valuable. The paper aims to optimize nuclear load following under stochastic demand and operational constraints.
method: The production decision is formulated as a finite-horizon optimal switching problem, with value functions characterized as viscosity solutions of HJB quasi-variational inequalities. A monotone semi-Lagrangian scheme is used to compute optimal policies.
result: Numerical results show how shortage costs, switching costs, ramping capability, and market access shape optimal nuclear load following, highlighting the economic value of controllable low-carbon capacity.
conclusion: The analysis provides implications for flexibility remuneration, balancing-market design, and interconnection policy in renewable-intensive systems.

title: A Volumetrically Stabilized Mixed Formulation Of The Finite Element Immersed Boundary Method For Fluid Structure Interaction With Fully Incompressible Hyperelastic Solids
authors: Paul T. Bauman Abhishek Mishra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The finite element immersed boundary method (FE IBM) with a distributed Lagrange multiplier is an attractive framework for fluid structure interaction (FSI) because it couples an Eulerian description of an incompressible fluid to a Lagrangian description of an immersed solid on two independent, nonconforming meshes, avoiding the costly remeshing required by body fitted arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian methods. When the immersed solid is modelled as a fully incompressible hyperelastic material, however, a direct finite element discretization of the deviatoric solid stress fails to enforce the Lagrangian incompressibility constraint, and the computed structure exhibits spurious volumetric instabilities and locking. In this work we present a mixed formulation of the distributed Lagrange multiplier FEIBM that restores volumetric stability. Following the theory of nearly incompressible hyperelasticity, we augment the solid stress with a volumetric contribution derived from a dilatational strain energy and introduce an additional solid pressure field, enforced weakly, that plays the role of the Lagrange multiplier for the Lagrangian incompressibility constraint J = 1. The resulting formulation is discretized in space by finite elements and in time by an unconditionally stable semi implicit scheme, and is implemented as a reusable Immersed Boundary physics kernel within the GRINS multiphysics framework, built on the libMesh finite element library. The method is verified on three FSI benchmarks, an elliptically displaced thick ring returning to equilibrium, a radially stretched incompressible ring, and a disk falling under gravity in a viscous fluid, for which the mixed formulation removes the volumetric failure observed with the unstabilized formulation and reproduces the analytical terminal velocity of the falling disk to within 1%.
tldr: This paper presents a mixed finite element formulation for the immersed boundary method to stabilize fluid-structure interaction with incompressible hyperelastic solids.
motivation: The paper addresses numerical instabilities (volumetric locking) in the finite element immersed boundary method when modeling fully incompressible hyperelastic solids.
method: It introduces a mixed formulation with an additional solid pressure field to enforce the incompressibility constraint, discretized with finite elements and a semi-implicit time scheme.
result: The method is verified on three benchmarks, removing volumetric failure and reproducing analytical terminal velocity within 1%.
conclusion: The proposed mixed formulation effectively stabilizes the FEIBM for incompressible hyperelastic solids, enabling accurate FSI simulations.

title: Towards Co-Designed Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking
authors: Roberto Luo, Pedro Henrique Silva Coutinho, Victor Hugo Pereira Rodrigues, Tiago Roux Oliveira, Miroslav Krstic
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies event-triggered gradient-based multivariable extremum seeking for nonlinear maps with polytopic Hessian uncertainty. Unlike existing event-triggered extremum-seeking methods, which first fix the controller (typically diagonal) and then design the triggering mechanism, the proposed approach jointly synthesizes the controller and the triggering mechanism through a co-design framework that admits both diagonal and full controller gain matrices. The co-design problem is formulated as a convex optimization problem with linear matrix inequality constraints. Its solution guarantees exponential convergence of the average closed-loop system with a prescribed decay rate while maximizing the admissible triggering threshold to reduce communication. Lyapunov and averaging analyses establish exponential stability of the event-triggered system, and Zeno-freeness is proved to guarantee implementability. Numerical results illustrate that diagonal gains cannot achieve the same triggering thresholds and decay rates as the full controller gain matrices, highlighting the benefits of exploiting Hessian coupling information.
tldr: This paper presents a co-design framework for event-triggered extremum seeking control, focusing on nonlinear maps with polytopic Hessian uncertainty.
motivation: Existing event-triggered extremum-seeking methods fix the controller and then design the triggering mechanism, which may not be optimal. The authors aim to jointly synthesize both to improve performance and reduce communication.
method: The co-design problem is formulated as a convex optimization with linear matrix inequality constraints, and Lyapunov and averaging analyses establish exponential stability and Zeno-freeness.
result: Numerical results show that full controller gain matrices achieve higher triggering thresholds and decay rates than diagonal gains, exploiting Hessian coupling information.
conclusion: The proposed co-design approach offers a systematic way to design event-triggered extremum seeking controllers with guaranteed stability and communication reduction.

title: Limit Theorems For A Class Of Martingale Arrays With Applications In Nonlinear Cointergating Regression
authors: Qiying Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a new asymptotic theory for a broad class of martingales, establishing convergence to limiting distributions that involve a functional of stochastic integrals. The proposed limit theorem substantially extends existing martingale asymptotic theory by accommodating a wider class of dependence structures. As a primary application, the theory is applied to nonlinear regression models with nonstationary time series, yielding a rigorous framework for asymptotic inference on nonlinear least square estimators.
tldr: This paper develops limit theorems for martingale arrays and applies them to nonlinear cointegrating regression, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to extend martingale asymptotic theory to handle broader dependence structures, enabling inference in nonlinear regression with nonstationary time series.
method: The author establishes new limit theorems for a class of martingale arrays, deriving convergence to distributions involving stochastic integrals, and applies them to nonlinear least squares estimators.
result: The proposed theorems generalize existing martingale asymptotics and provide a rigorous framework for asymptotic inference in nonlinear cointegrating regression.
conclusion: The paper contributes to econometrics and time series analysis, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information science.

title: Attainment Boundaries And Escape Rates In Asymptotically Conic Optimization
authors: Vinh Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.10341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study attainment boundaries for linear optimization over unbounded convex sets. For epigraphs of finite convex functions, convex conjugacy separates recession-cone copositivity, boundedness below, and attainment through three nested subsets of conjugate space. At a finite but unattained boundary value, we establish a facewise asymptotic selection theorem for inward perturbations of the objective. The theorem identifies the escaping directions of the perturbed minimizers, their precise blow-up scale, and the leading asymptotics of the optimal value; the critical set may be multidimensional, and no radial symmetry is assumed. For radial asymptotically conic epigraphs, we obtain a complete boundary trichotomy and universal scaling laws for objective tilting, hard truncation, and power regularization. For shifted ellipsoidal second-order cone programs, we derive explicit primal--dual formulas together with sharp escape, conditioning, and regularization rates.
